title: arXiv Trending Physics — Daily — Friday, 13 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This is an inferred ranking of notable recent papers, not a popularity measure; citation evidence is too sparse for these new papers to support a reliable popularity ordering.

sections.title: Observation of the $\Lambda(1520)$ suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV
sections.abstract: ALICE measures a central-to-peripheral reduction of the Λ(1520)/Λ yield ratio in 5.02 TeV Pb-Pb collisions and compares the centrality trend with hadronization and transport models.
sections.claimed_result: ALICE reports a 59% central-to-peripheral suppression (Rcp=0.411 ± 0.015 stat ± 0.086 syst); MUSIC coupled to the SMASH hadronic afterburner reproduces the trend within uncertainties.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE Pb-Pb collision data at √sNN=5.02 TeV, compared with statistical-hadronization and hydrodynamic-plus-transport calculations
sections.unique_caveat: The 8.6% systematic uncertainty is material, and the model comparison supports late-stage hadronic effects without independently separating rescattering from regeneration.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The collaboration reports a 6.8σ suppression significance and calls this the first above-5σ observation of resonance suppression within one collision system; submitted to PRL and measured in six centrality classes.

sections.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
sections.abstract: The authors derive a three-time witness for quantum memory that pairwise tests miss and demonstrate the hierarchy in a time-continuous superconducting-qubit experiment.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct a qubit dynamics for which every pair of times admits a classical-memory explanation, but a joint three-time witness certifies quantum memory.
sections.evidence_type: experimental and theoretical; analytical witness and channel tomography in a time-continuous superconducting-qubit realization with time-independent couplings
sections.unique_caveat: Demonstrated on one qubit platform; the authors note that proving higher-k memory becomes harder because every lower-order subdynamics must also admit a classical decomposition.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A new analytical witness is tested on a superconducting-qubit platform, and the result received paper-specific discussion at Quantum.world.

sections.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate an entanglement-based quantum-key-distribution network over deployed Slovak telecommunication fiber, with four cities connected and keys delivered after full post-processing.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 13.5 bit/s over 109 km and 4.3 bit/s over a 142.9 km link with 32.1 dB loss; their analysis finds the implemented scheme does not certify a finite key on the longest link.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; deployed Slovak fiber network, entangled-photon source, simultaneous link operation, and complete post-processing with real-time delivery
sections.unique_caveat: The authors warn that heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound for short blocks, so finite-size corrections are required before delivered keys can be considered secure; the longest link has no certified key under the implemented scheme.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A deployed multi-city network and delivered-key rates were covered by Quantum.world and Quantum Zeitgeist; the paper benchmarks the full processing chain against finite-key bounds.

sections.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
sections.abstract: Three JWST/MIRI eclipse visits, combined with prior spectra and radial velocities, indicate that nearby rocky planet LTT 1445 A b has no substantial atmosphere, while its sibling planet c remains weakly constrained.
sections.claimed_result: For planet b, the authors infer CO2 partial pressure below 0.6 mbar and surface pressure of about 0.1 bar or less; for c, they rule out only thick CO2-bearing atmospheres.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST MIRI/F1500W secondary eclipses, archival JWST spectra, and a joint fit including 220 radial velocities
sections.unique_caveat: Planet c’s potentially grazing eclipse and overlapping events leave its depth poorly constrained; planet b’s atmospheric limits depend on retrieval and forward-model assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three independent data reductions and a joint fit strengthen the measurement; the preprint received paper-specific discussion at Pith and science-media coverage.

sections.title: Euclid data release 1 (DR1) - SIR spectroscopic calibration
sections.abstract: The Euclid SIR paper describes calibration pipelines for the mission’s slitless spectra and reports that DR1 products meet current wavelength- and flux-calibration requirements.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that DR1’s calibration products meet mission requirements while identifying pipeline improvements for later releases.
sections.evidence_type: observational and computational; Euclid/NISP slitless spectroscopy and SIR calibration products
sections.unique_caveat: This is calibration readiness, not a new cosmological constraint; residual calibration systematics can propagate into wavelength and flux measurements, and the paper lists optimizations still in progress.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper underpins Euclid DR1’s reported 170-million-plus validated spectra, is tied to the ESA DR1 release, and is submitted to A&A.

sections.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
sections.abstract: Multiwavelength observations of a black-hole X-ray binary outburst suggest that a vertically extended inner disk can shield the outer disk even at about 0.2 of the Eddington luminosity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret the outburst-peak spectrum and its evolution as evidence for an expanded inner disk that self-shadows the outer regions at sub-Eddington luminosity.
sections.evidence_type: observational; multiwavelength spectroscopy during an X-ray binary outburst, supported by contemporaneous X-ray spectra
sections.unique_caveat: The inference is based on one outburst; the authors’ suggestion that self-shadowing is common requires comparison with further systems and states.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record reports publication in Nature Astronomy (DOI 10.1038/s41550-026-03005-2); contemporaneous X-ray spectra support the optical/infrared interpretation.

sections.title: Detection of 2 MeV spectral bump and ~40 MeV emission line from GRB 221009A
sections.abstract: The authors combine unsaturated CSES-01/HEPP-H measurements with GECAM-C and Fermi data to reconstruct GRB 221009A’s spectrum from 2 to 255 MeV, reporting a MeV bump and a time-evolving emission line.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a spectral bump near 2 MeV and a line near 40 MeV whose energy declines approximately as (t-t0)^-1.05, interpreting the combined features as evidence for a structured, magnetically dominated jet.
sections.evidence_type: observational; CSES-01/HEPP-H measurements cross-calibrated with GECAM-C and Fermi gamma-ray data
sections.unique_caveat: The jet interpretation is model-dependent; the paper reports comparable fits for different continuum components, and the reconstructed spectrum relies on instrument-response and cross-calibration modeling.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The preprint is accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters and combines CSES-01/HEPP-H with GECAM-C and Fermi observations across a difficult energy range.

sections.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
sections.abstract: Mid-infrared pumping of NiO produces a finite-momentum two-magnon signal whose decay is much slower than previously reported two-magnon coherence times.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a light-induced bimagnon signal in NiO, with its spectral weight peaking about 4 ps after pumping and a decay time of 28 ± 11 ps.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; mid-infrared pump and time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at finite momentum
sections.unique_caveat: The delayed growth is resolved well beyond the 0.5 ps time resolution, but the proposed momentum redistribution explanation is an interpretation rather than direct observation of the redistribution process.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports a measured 28 ± 11 ps decay and is cross-listed across four physics subfields, linking magnetic excitations, optical driving, materials, and quantum physics.

sections.title: Characterising a population of fast-declining SNe Ia in galaxy cluster cores
sections.abstract: An analysis of ZTF transients finds that photometrically selected Type Ia supernova candidates in cluster cores have faster light-curve declines than comparison populations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find a roughly 4σ difference in light-curve stretch for the core sample versus outer-core and field populations, and suggest progenitor age may contribute to SN Ia diversity.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Zwicky Transient Facility archival light curves selected and analyzed with the AMPEL platform
sections.unique_caveat: The candidates are photometrically identified, and the preference for a bimodal rather than unimodal distribution is marginal (ΔAIC 1.53 and 2.3); the progenitor interpretation is not a direct measurement.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors analyze 89,025 ZTF transients and identify 242 likely cluster-core SNe Ia; a science-media summary discusses the reported population difference.

sections.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
sections.abstract: A self-consistent population-synthesis fit to Gaia DR3 main-sequence and white-dwarf stars favors an early-peaking, subsequently declining Milky Way star-formation history with two later bursts.
sections.claimed_result: Their 18-parameter CALOMERA fit reproduces star counts within 3% in each colour-magnitude region and recovers two recent star-formation bursts near 2.4 and 0.5 Gyr ago.
sections.evidence_type: computational and observational; Gaia DR3 sample calibrated with a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population model and three white-dwarf cooling libraries
sections.unique_caveat: The inferred history depends on stellar-evolution and cooling prescriptions; the authors report that cooling-library differences are concentrated at the faint end (MG ≳ 15).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors fit 7.98 million Gaia DR3 stars, including 110,000 white dwarfs; submitted to MNRAS and cross-listed across Galactic and stellar astrophysics.

sections.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$\alpha$ Forest at the Field Level
sections.abstract: A cubic-order perturbative forward model for the Lyman-α forest is validated against hydrodynamic simulations and used to estimate nonlinear shifts in baryon acoustic oscillation parameters.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report about 5% agreement in the 3D flux power spectrum over tested scales and predict sub-percent radial and transverse BAO shifts that vary with cosmology and redshift.
sections.evidence_type: computational; cubic-order effective-field-theory model validated on CAMELS and Sherwood simulations
sections.unique_caveat: These are simulation-based predictions and priors, not a new BAO measurement from DESI; applicability depends on the forward model and simulation coverage.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The model is tested against both CAMELS and Sherwood hydrodynamic simulations, improves agreement over earlier quadratic models, and targets DESI/DESI-II analyses.

sections.title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
sections.abstract: The authors present a GPU-enabled sampler for jointly inferring overlapping LISA sources and instrumental noise, testing it on simulated Galactic-binary datasets.
sections.claimed_result: The authors demonstrate source reconstruction from empty initial models for 143- and 866-binary simulations and computational feasibility in a separate 16,435-binary stress test initialized at injected parameters.
sections.evidence_type: computational; C++/CUDA trans-dimensional sampler tested on simulated LISA datasets with Galactic white-dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian noise
sections.unique_caveat: The largest stress test starts from injected parameters, and the authors identify incomplete mixing and source-count uncertainty as outstanding issues; this is not an analysis of observed LISA data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A one-year simulated-data stress test explores 16,435 binaries (131,480 source parameters) and reports 15 million iterations in about 16 hours using about 3 GB RAM.
